# Marquee ring example

Five relay nodes plus a supervisor root:

```text
. ──submit──▶ a ──▶ b ──▶ c ──▶ d ──▶ e ──▶ a ──▶ …
```

Each hop is one Pi session that runs three steps — append its letter to
`ring.log`, relay the `ROUND N` baton to the next node, `swarm_complete` —
then the session reclaims itself (pi-onlyne ≥ 0.8.0 exits on the scheduler's
recycle signal and acks). Node e bumps the counter (`ROUND N+1`), so one
submission keeps the ring turning. Dead terminals and stalled `swarm_ready`
replay the task whole (attempt+1) with no cap — the root
`swarm.workspace.jsonc` carries `"retry": { "max_attempts": 0 }`.

The example exercises reclaim, relay, cycle, and unbounded replay on real
sessions while each prompt stays small enough to audit in one screen.

## Layout

Everything generated by `onlyne-swarm run` is gitignored; the repo keeps the
templates. `.ws/<node>/.pi/*` and `.ws/<node>/prompts/*` ship with the
example because `sync` never writes over instance Pi configuration.

```text
marquee/
  .agents/.schedule/{a..e}/template.workspace.jsonc   # role per node (the only job text)
  .onlyne/swarm.workspace.jsonc                       # root supervisor role + retry policy
  .onlyne/config.toml                                 # loopback-only daemon config, [swarm] on
  .pi/{settings.json,onlyne.json}                     # root Pi packages + watch settings
  .ws/{a..e}/.pi/settings.json                        # defaultTools: ["bash"], pinned pi-onlyne
  .ws/{a..e}/.pi/onlyne.json                          # swarm_prompt -> local wrapper
  .ws/{a..e}/prompts/swarm-task.md                    # node-specific injection wrapper
  prompts/swarm-task.md                               # root wrapper
  payload/round.md                                    # canonical ROUND 1 baton
```

## Run

The scheduler spawns one `onlyne` daemon per workspace and one Orca tab per
hop, so it needs `onlyne`, `orca`, `pi`, and a configured model. Keep the
swarm root on a short path (macOS Unix-socket limit):

```bash
cp -R examples/marquee /tmp/marquee
cd /tmp/marquee
onlyne-swarm run                 # syncs .schedule, generates .ws runtimes
onlyne-swarm submit --to a --payload payload/round.md
tail -f ring.log                 # a b c d e a b c d e …
```

Watch and stop the ring:

```bash
onlyne-swarm status              # states + counts per task
onlyne-swarm tui                 # live tree, ledger
onlyne-swarm cancel <task-id>    # cancel the current head task to stop
```

`cancel` signals the running session to recycle itself, waits for the
`swarm_recycled` ack, and closes the Orca tab. No shell injection: the
session exits by its own hand.
